findings.summary: The normalization call is gated backwards: `lift.method ? normalizeLift(lift) : lift` runs normalizeLift only when a lift already has a method (where it's a no-op passthrough) and skips it precisely for legacy lifts with no method — the exact case the brief calls out as needing normalizeLift's default-method derivation. Legacy lifts are written to the DB with no `method` field at all, so imported older exports are left in the non-normalized shape the task required them to leave in a consistent, fully-populated shape. Should be `snapshot.lifts.map(lift => normalizeLift(lift))` (normalizeLift already internally branches on lift.method, so the outer ternary is redundant as well as inverted). Verified by running the diff's own test suite: `a legacy lift (no method) is restored with a derived linear method` fails with `expected undefined to be 'linear'` (1 of 7 tests fail). This directly contradicts the implementer report's claim that tests were written and run — the suite is currently red.
